Exorcise

EK-sor-size · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To exorcise to drive out or expel, especially an evil spirit.

The priest was called to exorcise the spirit that villagers believed haunted the old chapel.

Worked Example

Years later, she finally exorcised the memory of the accident by returning to the site and facing it head-on.

Exorcise most literally means driving out an evil spirit, but it's also used figuratively for finally getting rid of a fear, memory, or bad habit that has haunted someone.

Strength Check

Word Choice

Exorcise is a dramatic, often religious or spiritual word -- for a casual everyday feeling like stress or a bad memory, 'get rid of' sounds far more natural than exorcise.
